fullPassage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push — essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work. And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains.

❌ ② 불일치: 'how to interact with technologies rather than how they work' — 기술의 작동 원리가 아닌 상호작용하는 법을 전달
❌ ③ 불일치: 'a small piece of a giant calculation' — 큰 두뇌를 거대한 계산의 작은 조각에 바친다고 함. 전체에 바치는 것이 아님
✅ ④ 일치: 'all we have to do is socially learn the right answers' — 올바른 답을 사회적으로 배우면 된다는 본문과 정확히 일치 ←정답
det.tip: socially learn the right answers = 올바른 답을 사회적으로 학습하다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② transmitting → transmitted: 수동태 be + p.p. 필요
det.analysis:
❌ ① recognizing: 'won his Nobel Prize for recognizing' — 전치사 for 뒤 동명사 정상
✅ ② transmitting: 'All that needs to be transmitting' — 수동태 needs to be + p.p.(transmitted)이 필요. transmitting(현재분사)은 수동태 구조에 부적합 ←정답
❌ ③ well: 'understand things well enough to benefit' — 부사 well이 동사 understand 수식, 정상
❌ ④ collective: 'our societies' collective brains' — 형용사가 명사 brains 수식, 정상
det.tip: needs to be transmitted = 전달될 필요가 있다 (수동태). needs to be transmitting은 진행 수동이 되어 문맥 오류

❌ ② works: 'how your computer or toilet works' — 주어 'your computer or toilet'(단수 취급) + works(3인칭 단수), 정상
❌ ③ holding: 'instead of holding more information' — 전치사 of 뒤 동명사, 정상
✅ ④ collectively: 'our societies' collectively brains' — 명사 brains를 수식하려면 형용사 collective이 필요. 부사 collectively는 명사 수식 불가 ←정답

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ done → doing: 진행형 be + 현재분사 필요
det.analysis:
❌ ① compute: 'lack the resources to compute answers' — to부정사 내 동사원형, 정상
❌ ② which: 'All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push' — 간접의문문의 의문형용사 which, 정상
❌ ③ making: 'we are making small calculations' — 현재진행형 are + making, 정상
✅ ④ done: 'We are just done our part' — 현재진행형 are + doing이 필요. done(과거분사)은 'are done = 끝났다'라는 다른 의미. 여기서는 '역할을 하고 있는 중'이므로 doing이 맞음 ←정답
det.tip: are doing our part = 우리의 역할을 하고 있다(진행). are done = 끝났다(완료). 문맥상 진행이 맞으므로 doing 필요

questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push — essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work. And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. __________.

[조건] (1) a, are, brains, collective, computation, doing, for, in, just, larger, our, our, part, societies', we를 모두 사용 (2) 15단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains

det.tip: doing our part = 우리의 역할을 하다. in a larger computation = 더 큰 계산에서. for our societies' collective brains = 사회의 집단 두뇌를 위해

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 interface(인터페이스)가 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① button: 버튼 — 뒤 문장에서 별도로 언급. '~를 사용하고 물을 내리다'의 맥락에서 버튼보다 인터페이스가 적합
✅ ② interface: 인터페이스 — 컴퓨터나 화장실의 작동 원리 대신 인터페이스를 사용하면 된다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ③ technology: 기술 — 너무 포괄적이고 and flush와 병렬 구조에 부적합
❌ ④ computation: 계산 — 화장실에 계산을 사용한다는 것은 문맥상 부적합
det.tip: use the interface and flush = 인터페이스를 사용하고 물을 내리다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 benefit from(이익을 얻다)가 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① contribute to: 기여하다 — 뒤에서 별도로 사용됨. '충분히 이해하여 ~하다'의 맥락에서 이익을 얻다가 적합
❌ ② interact with: 상호작용하다 — 앞 문장에서 기술과의 상호작용 맥락이며 여기서는 부적합
✅ ③ benefit from: 이익을 얻다 — 충분히 잘 이해하여 이익을 얻는다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ④ dedicate to: 바치다 — 앞 문장에서 이미 사용. 이해하여 바친다는 의미 부적합
det.tip: benefit from = ~로부터 이익을 얻다. well enough to benefit from = 이익을 얻을 만큼 충분히 잘

questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our (A)[limitations / advantages] in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and (B)[flush / disassemble]. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push — essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work. And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation. We understand things well enough to (C)[suffer from / benefit from] them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) limitations=한계, (B) flush=물을 내리다, (C) benefit from=이익을 얻다
det.analysis:
✅ ① limitations — flush — benefit from: 원문 일치. 정보·시간·인지능력의 한계(limitations)를 인식했고, 인터페이스를 사용하고 물을 내리면(flush) 되며, 충분히 이해해서 이익을 얻는다(benefit from)는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ② advantages — flush — benefit from: (A) advantages(이점)는 limitations(한계)의 반의어로 맥락 파괴
❌ ③ limitations — disassemble — benefit from: (B) disassemble(분해하다)은 flush(물을 내리다)와 전혀 다른 의미
❌ ④ limitations — flush — suffer from: (C) suffer from(고통받다)은 benefit from(이익을 얻다)의 반의어
det.tip: limitations(한계) / flush(물을 내리다) / benefit from(이익을 얻다)

questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers ①<u>independently</u>, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push — essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work. And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could ②<u>abandon</u> our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small ③<u>calculations</u> that contribute to a larger whole. We are just doing our part in a larger ④<u>computation</u> for our societies' collective brains.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② abandon → dedicate: 큰 두뇌를 바치다(dedicate), 포기하다(abandon) 아님
det.analysis:
❌ ① independently: 독립적으로 — 답을 독립적으로 계산할 자원이 부족하다는 맥락에 적절
✅ ② abandon: 포기하다 → dedicate(바치다) — 큰 두뇌를 작은 조각에 '바치다(전념하다)'가 원문. abandon(포기하다)은 맥락 파괴 ←정답
❌ ③ calculations: 계산 — 작은 계산을 하고 있다는 맥락에 적절
❌ ④ computation: 계산 — 더 큰 계산에서 역할을 한다는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: dedicate(바치다/전념하다) ↔ abandon(포기하다/버리다). 두뇌를 바치는 것이지 포기하는 것이 아님
